concepts.title: Types of Cellular Movement
concepts.definition: The three primary mechanisms by which human cells exhibit motion: amoeboid (using pseudopodia), ciliary (using hair-like projections), and muscular (using contractile proteins).
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Cells utilize different structural elements like microfilaments or cilia to reach internal or external movement.
question_patterns: what are the three types of movement in human cells
describe amoeboid movement in macrophages
where does ciliary movement occur in the human body
how do leucocytes move through the blood
what do you understand by types of cellular movement

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the cell is a macrophage, ciliated epithelial cell, or muscle cell.
Macrophages use amoeboid; respiratory tract uses ciliary; limbs use muscular movement.

solution_steps.action: verify the structural element driving the movement
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that amoeboid movement relies on microfilaments, ciliary movement on microtubules, and muscular movement on contractile actin-myosin proteins, validating the link between structure and function.

concepts.title: Classification of Muscle Tissues
concepts.definition: Muscles are specialized mesodermal tissues categorized into skeletal (striated/voluntary), visceral (smooth/involuntary), and cardiac (striated/involuntary) types.
concepts.key_idea: Muscles are distinguished by their location, microscopic appearance, and the nature of their nervous regulation.
question_patterns: classify muscles based on their location
what are the characteristics of visceral muscles
distinguish between skeletal and cardiac muscles
why are skeletal muscles called voluntary
justify why classification of muscle tissues matters

solution_steps.explain: Skeletal and cardiac muscles show stripes; visceral muscles are smooth.
Skeletal is voluntary; visceral and cardiac are involuntary.

solution_steps.action: verify muscle classification by location and regulation
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that skeletal muscles attach to bones for locomotion, visceral muscles line hollow organs for peristalsis, and cardiac muscles form the heart wall, validating the three-way classification by striation and control.

concepts.title: Structure of the Sarcomere
concepts.definition: The functional unit of a myofibril located between two successive Z-lines, containing organized arrangements of actin and myosin filaments.
concepts.key_idea: The sarcomere is indeed the basic contractile segment that shortens during muscle activity.
question_patterns: define a sarcomere
what is the H-zone in a muscle fibre
identify the boundaries of a sarcomere
describe the arrangement of A and I bands
what do you understand by structure of the sarcomere

solution_steps.explain: Identify the elastic fibers that bisect the I-bands.
The A-band contains myosin; the I-band contains actin; the H-zone is the central myosin-only part.

solution_steps.action: verify the sarcomere shortens during contraction
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that during contraction the I-band and H-zone narrow while the A-band stays constant, validating the sliding filament model where actin filaments slide over myosin toward the sarcomere center.

concepts.title: Sliding Filament Theory Mechanism
concepts.definition: The process where muscle contraction occurs by thin actin filaments sliding over thick myosin filaments, triggered by neural signals and calcium release.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: ATP hydrolysis powers the myosin head to form cross-bridges with actin, pulling them toward the center.
question_patterns: explain the sliding filament theory
role of calcium ions in muscle contraction
what happens to the I-band during contraction
how is a cross-bridge formed
short note on sliding filament theory mechanism

solution_steps.explain: CNS sends signal via motor neuron to release Acetylcholine.
Calcium binds to troponin, exposing active sites on actin.
Myosin head binds to actin using ATP and pulls the filament.

concepts.title: Axial Skeleton Bone Count
concepts.definition: The skeleton's central part - skull, sternum, ribs and the vertebral column - 80 bones in all.
concepts.formula: total_axial = skull + hyoid + ossicles + vertebrae + sternum + ribs
concepts.key_idea: The axial skeleton is made up of 80 bones aligned along the body's main longitudinal axis.
question_patterns: calculate the total bones in the axial skeleton
how many bones make up the human skull
find the number of bones in the axial system
what is the sum of cranial and facial bones
solve a numerical on axial skeleton bone count

solution_steps.explain: Skull has 8 cranial and 14 facial bones.
Add 1 hyoid and 6 ear ossicles to the skull count.
Add 26 vertebrae, 1 sternum, and 24 ribs.

concepts.title: Vertebral Column Composition
concepts.definition: The series of 26 bone units protecting the spinal cord, divided into cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, and coccygeal regions.
concepts.formula: total_v = cervical + thoracic + lumbar + sacral + coccygeal
concepts.key_idea: Human vertebrae are regionally specialized, with a constant number of 7 cervical vertebrae in most mammals.
question_patterns: calculate the total number of vertebrae
how many thoracic vertebrae are in humans
what is the sum of cervical and lumbar vertebrae
find the total vertebrae count
what is the result in this vertebral column composition problem

solution_steps.explain: Cervical(7), Thoracic(12), Lumbar(5), Sacral(1), Coccygeal(1).

solution_steps.action: substitute the regional vertebrae counts into the formula
solution_steps.explain: Insert the standard vertebral counts for each region into the total vertebrae formula to obtain the sum for the entire vertebral column.

solution_steps.action: compute and state the final vertebral column count
solution_steps.explain: Perform the addition to confirm the vertebral column comprises 26 bones, validating the regional specialization along the body's main axis.

concepts.title: Rib Cage Structure
concepts.definition: The protective enclosure of the thorax formed by the sternum, thoracic vertebrae, and 12 pairs of ribs.
concepts.key_idea: Ribs are indeed classified as true, false, or floating using their attachment to the sternum.
question_patterns: calculate the total number of ribs
how many floating ribs are there
what is the total of true and false ribs
find the number of rib bones in a human
find the required value in a rib cage structure problem

solution_steps.explain: There are 7 pairs of true ribs.
There are 3 pairs of false ribs (8th, 9th, 10th).
There are 2 pairs of floating ribs.
Total ribs is the sum of all three types.

concepts.title: Appendicular Skeleton (Limb Bones)
concepts.definition: The bones of the arms and legs together with their supporting both pectoral and pelvic girdles.
concepts.key_idea: Each of the four human limbs contains exactly 30 bones.
question_patterns: how many bones are in one human limb
calculate the total bones in both hands
find the number of phalanges in one limb
what is the total bone count of the appendicular skeleton
what is the result in this appendicular skeleton (limb bones) problem

solution_steps.explain: Humerus(1), Radius(1), Ulna(1), Carpals(8), Metacarpals(5), Phalanges(14).
Femur(1), Tibia(1), Fibula(1), Patella(1), Tarsals(7), Metatarsals(5), Phalanges(14).

solution_steps.action: compute and state the total limb bone count
solution_steps.explain: Add the hand and leg bone counts to confirm each limb contains 30 bones, validating that all four limbs together hold 120 bones of the appendicular skeleton.

concepts.title: Types of Joints
concepts.definition: Structural points of contact between bones categorized by their degree of mobility: fibrous (immovable), cartilaginous (semi-movable), and synovial (freely movable).
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Joints act as fulcrums for muscle-generated force to produce body movement.
question_patterns: classify joints based on mobility
give an example of a pivot joint
where are fibrous joints found
what type of joint is the knee
short note on types of joints

solution_steps.explain: Check if bones are fused by tissue, cartilage, or separated by a fluid cavity.
Sutures are fibrous; vertebrae are cartilaginous; limbs are synovial.

solution_steps.action: verify joint mobility matches its functional role
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that fibrous joints provide stability (skull sutures), cartilaginous joints allow limited movement (intervertebral discs), and synovial joints permit free movement (knee, elbow), validating the link between joint structure and mobility.

concepts.title: Musculoskeletal Disorders
concepts.definition: Clinical conditions affecting the muscles and bones, including autoimmune, genetic, and age-related diseases.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Disorders like both osteoporosis and arthritis significantly impact bone density and joint function.
question_patterns: what is myasthenia gravis
cause of osteoporosis in elderly women
distinguish between arthritis and gout
what causes tetany
short note on musculoskeletal disorders

solution_steps.explain: Check for low calcium (tetany), uric acid (gout), or estrogen (osteoporosis).

solution_steps.action: classify the disorder by underlying mechanism
solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the disorder is autoimmune (myasthenia gravis), metabolic (gout, tetany), genetic (muscular dystrophy), or age-related (osteoporosis, arthritis).

solution_steps.action: verify the disorder's impact on musculoskeletal function
solution_steps.explain: Confirm how the disease affects muscle weakness, bone density loss, or joint inflammation, validating the clinical significance of each musculoskeletal disorder.
